findings.title: SOQL Injection in dynamic query
findings.explanation: The method concatenates the user‑supplied searchKey directly into a dynamic SOQL string without escaping or binding, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SOQL clauses and potentially read or modify data beyond their permissions.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the query to use bind variables or escape the input: e.g., `String query = 'SELECT Id, Name, Industry FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE :searchKey LIMIT 50';` or use `Database.queryWithBinds`. Ensure the searchKey is sanitized with `String.escapeSingleQuotes` if dynamic construction is unavoidable.

findings.title: Field-Level Security Violation in Contact Query
findings.explanation: The method queries the Contact record for the Birthdate and Email fields without enforcing field‑level security. The permission set explicitly denies read access to Birthdate, so a user with this permission set can retrieve sensitive data they should not see.
findings.remediation: Add FLS enforcement to the query, e.g., use `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` or `Security.stripInaccessible` after the query, or remove the sensitive fields from the SELECT clause. Ensure that any fields queried are granted read permission in the permission set or profile.

findings.title: Record-level sharing bypass in @AuraEnabled method
findings.explanation: The class is declared "without sharing", so record-level sharing rules are ignored. Because the method is exposed via @AuraEnabled, any user with the permission set can invoke it and retrieve cases they should not see, bypassing sharing restrictions.
findings.remediation: Declare the class with "with sharing" or "inherited sharing", or add a WITH SHARE clause to the SOQL query. This ensures that only records the user is allowed to see are returned.

findings.title: Excessive permissions in Support Agent Tools permission set
findings.explanation: The permission set grants ModifyAllData and ViewAllData, which allow users to bypass all sharing and field-level security on every object. This far exceeds the described purpose of only viewing and closing cases.
findings.remediation: Remove the ModifyAllData and ViewAllData permissions from the permission set. Grant only the necessary Case object permissions (Read, Edit) and any other minimal permissions required for the support agent role.

findings.title: Field-Level Security Violation
findings.explanation: The SOQL query returns the Name field, but the Guest User profile does not grant read permission for Contact.Name. Apex runs in system mode and ignores FLS unless explicitly enforced, so the guest user can see data they should not.
findings.remediation: Enforce FLS by adding WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED to the query or by using Security.stripInaccessible to remove disallowed fields. Alternatively, remove the Name field from the query if it is not required.

findings.title: Record-Level Sharing Bypass
findings.explanation: The class is declared "without sharing", so record-level sharing rules are ignored. The Guest User profile can therefore read all Contact records, regardless of sharing settings.
findings.remediation: Declare the class with "with sharing" or use WITH USER_MODE in the SOQL query to enforce sharing rules.

findings.title: Guest User Exposure to Sensitive Data
findings.explanation: The Guest User profile has access to the @AuraEnabled method, allowing unauthenticated users to invoke it and retrieve contact information.
findings.remediation: Remove the class from the Guest User profile, restrict @AuraEnabled methods to authenticated users, or implement additional checks to ensure only intended data is returned.
